mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates indicate tight monetary policy, leading to decreased corporate borrowing and investment, which negatively impacts S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when FEDFUNDS is high, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts reflects strong consumer demand, signaling economic expansion and positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns are negative when HOUST exceeds 2000, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment indicates a strong labor market, but may signal inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Positive returns when UNRATE is low, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production suggests economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Negative returns with high INDPRO, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth exceeds inflation, real economic growth is positive, leading to higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Negative returns when GDPC1 > CPIAUCSL, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates increase borrowing costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Positive returns when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing employment with decreasing retail sales indicates economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Positive returns with PAYEMS up and RSAFS down, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment during expansion signals a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Negative returns with low UNRATE, or Rank IC < 0.03.
